rubric.criterion: The reviewer rejects alerting as one branch and recursively separates policy mutation, observation evaluation, incident transition, and external delivery lifecycles; SPLIT is an intermediate routing result rather than the final report.
Child lifecycles are reviewed sequentially, using a fresh context and compact parent handoff when the agent environment supports it.

The reviewer uses ast-grep when available to enumerate definitions, callers, state writes, and external-effect boundaries, then reads the matched control flow; ripgrep is used for lexical discovery rather than as semantic proof.
Each child records its public input, complete transition or algorithm, canonical and derived state, external effects, failure paths, and dominant work before receiving a verdict.
A child receives DESCEND only after the complete trace supports it; incomplete children remain SPLIT or UNPROVEN.
UNPROVEN is reserved for evidence that remains unavailable after an explicit inspection attempt, not for accessible child lifecycles the reviewer deferred.
The reviewer does not infer the design of one child from a representative file belonging to another child.
